Sri Gangala Bhoomaiah vs The State Of Telangana on 16
February, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.4460 of 2023
Order:

entities.text: Gangala Bhoomaiah vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Writ Petition is filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief, viz., "... ... ... to issue writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS declaring to the without any notice for road widening from Sidda Rameshwara temple comman to police station in between the petitioner house no 8-112/1 for admeasuring 188 72 sq yards with existing building with permission from the Gram Panchayat No GPB/31/18 dt 22 10 2018 and setbacks again extending the 90 feets to 110 feets without any land acquisition proceedings and trying to road widening on dt 09 02 2023 by demolishing the petitioner building without due processes of law as illegal arbitrary and violation Article -14 and 21 300-A of the Constitution of India... ..."

2. Heard Mr.K. Buchi Babu, learned counsel for the petitioner; the learned Government Pleader for Panchayat Raj, for respondent Nos.1, 3 and 4; Mr. R. Chandra Shekar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for Biknoor Gram Panchayat, for respondent Nos.5 and 6.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that petitioner herein is the absolute owner and possessor of House bearing No.8-112/1, admeasuring 188.72 Sq.yds., ::2:: CVBR,J wp_4460_2023 situate at Biknoor Village and Mandal, Kamareddy District; subsequently, the petitioner obtained building permission from respondent Nos.5 and 6 vide permit No.GPB/31/18, dated 22.10.2018,
and constructed a building in the subject property strictly in accordance with the permission;
however, the respondent-Authorities, without following the provisions laid down under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013, are forcibly trying to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property on the ground that the subject property is required for the purpose of road- widening; and therefore, prayed this Court to pass appropriate orders in the Writ Petition by directing the respondents not to interfere with the subject property of the petitioner, and allow the Writ Petition.

In view of above submissions, this Court is of the considered view that the present Writ Petition can be disposed of by directing the respondents herein not to interfere with the petitioner's property or demolish the existing structures in the petitioner's property without following due process of law.
